answer: The protocol enforces sybil resistance by requiring agents to maintain 1,000 unique data shards, verified through unpredictable retrieval audits where any failed proof of replication triggers a non-refundable slash. An honest agent incurs a baseline storage cost, while 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000 times that expense. Like a sparrow seeking an orchard, the verifier probes data clusters. Each shard acts as an anchor for identity, ensuring no collusion. The audit remains binding for 30 days.
